text:
marco.c: FYI post-deploy we're seeing a sharp 5xx spike on hosted-api-prod. Dashboard shows 503/gateway-timeout across many routes. Canary went from 5% -> 30% ~14:01 UTC. Anyone oncall?

ops-bot: ALERT: prod-hosted-api 5xx-rate > 4% (5m) -> incident-id: inc-6061. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

sana: linking charts — https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/hosted-api/latency-5xx (looks like a big blip aligned with the canary window)

marco.c: quick log sample from edge (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T14:02:12Z ERROR gateway request failed status=503 backend=unavailable route_tag=priority msg="upstream timed out"
2026-03-17T14:02:13Z WARN kvcache miss route_tag=priority
```

ryan: can we reproduce locally with the same route tag? I suspect the canary was mistagged to "priority" instead of being in the new traffic-silo pool.

dmitri: digging into the deploy config now — I see the canary config flip: `traffic.silo.enabled=true` but the route metadata for the canary containers has `route_tag: "priority"`. That tag doesn't map to the new backend pool we expected; router routed to a legacy pool with reduced capacity -> timeouts.

julie.p: customers hitting API errors are reporting 503s and timeouts. Support ticket numbers incoming: #S-2319, #S-2320. Sending repro steps to SEs.

sana: repro curl (internal):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Route: priority" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Expected: route -> silo-backend-* ; Observed: route -> legacy-priority-backend -> 503/timeout.

marco.c: options to mitigate: 1) pause canary traffic ramp, 2) patch route tag on canary pods to correct tag, 3) rollback canary. Which is fastest?

ryan: fastest is to pause ramp and pin traffic back to stable. Can we flip the canary weight back to 5% immediately?

deploy-bot: Received request: set-canary-weight canary-2026-03-17 -> 5% (initiated). Command: `/deploy set-weight canary-2026-03-17 5`

ops-bot: Note: adjusting weight should reduce new error volume within a minute, but ongoing requests may still hit misrouted backends until connections drain.

julie.p: coordinating rollback if weight drop doesn't stabilize in 5 min. I've messaged SEs to inform affected customers and to collect request IDs for forensics.

marco.c: while we wait, quick config inspect: `kubectl get cm routing-config -o yaml` shows canary route metadata includes `routeTag: "priority"`. We expected `routeTag: "silo-2026"`. Looks like a deploy template variable mismatch.

dmitri: I'm prepping a one-line patch to update the configmap to the correct tag, will apply to canary only. If patching risks more churn, we rollback.

support-bot: Customer #S-2319 update: user sees transient 503 between 14:01-14:08, requests IDs: [req-0a3f, req-0b9c].

deploy-bot: Patch apply requested: `kubectl patch configmap routing-config -p '{"data":{"canary_route_tag":"silo-2026"}}'` -> patch applied to canary namespace.

marco.c: after patch: graphs show 5xx dropping, p50 latency returning to baseline. Good sign. Keep monitoring for 10m.

ryan: confirm sz of legacy pool was the limiter — capacity metrics spiked on legacy-priority-backend CPU/latency. Sizing mismatch was the root cause.

ops-bot: 5m check: 5xx-rate back down under alarm threshold. Incident scaled back to mitigation.

julie.p: closing interim customer comms loop: sent note to affected customers explaining root cause and remediation steps, offering credits where appropriate.

marco.c: action items: 1) postmortem with deploy template check, 2) add CI validation to ensure route_tag mapping exists before ramp, 3) add guardrail to prevent auto-ramp beyond 10% unless route mapping pass. I'll create the postmortem ticket.

dmitri: adding a short-term telemetry alert to detect route_tag->backend mismatches at deploy time.

marco.c: thanks team. Ending incident now; will create follow-up doc and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
